note: Headline readings of each tool page at its default specification, computed from the same snapshot. Price-dependent readings are recomputed live on the hub from the spot price.

metcalfe.spec: cumulative addresses, n², no lost-coin adjustment, fit 2017 onward

null_test.note: ln price regressed on ln days-since-genesis (time), on ln(users²/supply) (network), and on both, 2017 window; out-of-sample by expanding annual refits. network_vs_time compares the two single-regressor models; negative means the user stock predicted next year better than calendar time; the year-by-year range says how stable that is. Within this specification the user stock did not clearly outperform the simpler time model, and nothing here says the Metcalfe model fails. The joint model is reported because a reviewer asked for it, and its coefficients are not separately identified: the two regressors are near-collinear on a series that grows six orders of magnitude, which is why its out-of-sample error is worse than either alone. Descriptive, not causal: address counts respond to price as well as drive it.

powerlaw.spec: log10 P = a + β log10(days since genesis), from day 560

extended.note: Tier 1 metrics from series already in the snapshot; percentiles over the stated window at daily close. Descriptive, not signals; forward-return rows are in-sample with overlapping windows.

nvt.volume_source: blockchain.com estimated tx volume, not entity adjusted

fee_share.note: fees as a share of miner revenue; the long-run security-budget question

volatility.note: VRP = implied (DVOL) minus realized; persistently positive is normal, negative marks stress

coinbase_premium.note: Coinbase USD spot vs offshore USDT close (OKX); USDT peg deviation is inside this number

technical.note: current readings only; the historical record of these rules is on the technical-signals page

independence.note: Spearman rank correlation of daily levels since 2019 with midranks for ties. Pairs at or above 0.8 in absolute value are, for the purpose of counting evidence, one observation: several columns agreeing is not several confirmations. Levels are used rather than changes because the site's tables read states, not moves.
